root_cause.text: The vulnerability is caused by the BPF BTF subsystem referencing the obsolete `CONFIG_CFI_CLANG` configuration symbol instead of the renamed `CONFIG_CFI`, resulting in the Control Flow Integrity enforcement logic for destructor kfuncs being excluded during compilation.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff shows the correction from `IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_CFI_CLANG)` to `IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_CFI)` in `kernel/bpf/btf.c`, and the commit message explicitly states that using the wrong name results in the code getting compiled out, leaving CFI failures for `btf_dtor_kfunc_t` unhandled.

bic_trace_step.commit_msg:
bpf, btf: Enforce destructor kfunc type with CFI

Ensure that registered destructor kfuncs have the same type
as btf_dto
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 99fde4d0626176d03cea35c64a063df73816e64d
Author: Sami Tolvanen <samitolvanen@google.com>
Date:   Sat Jan 10 08:25:53 2026 +0000

    bpf, btf: Enforce destructor kfunc type with CFI
    
    Ensure that registered destructor kfuncs have the same type
    as btf_dtor_kfunc_t to avoid a kernel panic on systems with
    CONFIG_CFI enabled.
    
    Signed-off-by: Sami Tolvanen <samitolvanen@google.com>
    Acked-by: Yonghong Song <yonghong.song@linux.dev>
    Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/
bic_trace_step.reason: The commit diff shows the vulnerable construct clearly. Line '+if (IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_CFI_CLANG))' uses the obsolete CONFIG_CFI_CLANG symbol instead of the renamed CONFIG_CFI as stated in the vulnerability root cause. This causes the CFI enforcement logic for destructor kfuncs to be excluded during compilation when CONFIG_CFI is enabled but CONFIG_CFI_CLANG is not. The code does NOT contain any fix - it still references CONFIG_CFI_CLANG which is the root cause of the vulnerability. This is a Bug-Introducing Commit that added the CFI check but with the wrong configuration symbol.
